name: Koya Content Desk, Publishing Queue Tick

nodes.name: Every 5 minutes
nodes.notes: Five minutes is a deliberate choice, not a default. Scheduling granularity finer than this buys nothing for content publishing, and each tick is a request that costs something.

nodes.name: Resolve config
nodes.notes: Throws if either value is unreadable, which n8n reports as a failed execution rather than a tick that quietly ran unauthenticated. See the in-code comment for why this cannot simply be an {{ $env.X || $vars.X }} expression on the HTTP node instead.

nodes.name: Tick the queue
nodes.notes:
NEVER ERROR IS DELIBERATELY OFF.

The 'Never Error' option would make this node report success on a 500, which is precisely the silent failure this whole system is built to avoid. A failed tick must show as a failed execution.

Retrying is safe: the app claims rows with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and every queue row carries a UNIQUE idempotency key that is passed through to the provider. A retry after a timeout cannot double-post.

nodes.name: Does a person need to look?
nodes.notes: A quiet tick posts nothing. A channel notification on every successful 5-minute tick would bury the one that matters.

nodes.name: Format alert
nodes.notes: Blocked and failed are reported together but they are NOT the same thing: blocked means a channel has no credentials or an approval is no longer current (expected — the normal state for X when paid publishing is off); failed means the provider was reached and something went wrong, and someone should look. The per-item lines keep both in view.

nodes.name: Alert #content-errors
nodes.notes: Same credential as koya-notifications.json's error channel — reuse it rather than creating a second one, since both post to #content-errors. The webhook URL lives only in this credential, never in a workflow variable or in this node's own parameters.

main.node: Does a person need to look?
